title: SLA-driven model intake lanes and enterprise pinning triage
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, SLA-aware triage and intake workflow for enterprise model requests (new adds, version pinning, and deprecations) that reduces time-to-serve for high-priority customers while maintaining safety, license compliance, and quality guards.

Scope:
- Intake form + automated pre-checks (license scan, size & architecture compatibility, basic eval harness run)
- Three primary triage lanes: Fast-Track (SLA-backed enterprise requests), Standard Catalog (general public catalog additions), Evaluation/Pilot (experimental or research models)
- Pinning & deprecation policy: formal checklist for approval, rollback plan and sunset windows, automated notifications to customers pinned to versions
- Gate definitions: required eval metrics, allowed license types, security & privacy checklist, and performance delta thresholds for fallback decisions.

Proposed triage lanes (high-level):
1) SLA Fast-Track lane (enterprise):
   - Trigger: customer contract or support case marks request as SLA-fasttrack OR usage above commit threshold.
   - Requirements: full eval harness run (latency, throughput, quality regressions vs pinned baseline), license clearance (no incompatible restrictives), security scan pass, KMS compatibility verified.
   - Acceptance thresholds: quality regression <= 2% (task-specific metric) or within agreed exception; tail P95 latency <= 1.5x of baseline for target sequence lengths; max memory/quantization profile supported by Dedicated.
   - Owners: PM triage lead + ENG runtime owner + Solutions engineer.
2) Standard Catalog lane:
   - Trigger: community or internal request without SLA.
   - Requirements: simplified eval (smoke tests + representative eval set), license check, model card.
   - SLO: decision within 10 business days.
3) Evaluation/Pilot lane:
   - Trigger: research models, experimental quantizations, or models flagged for risk review.
   - Requirements: extended eval suite, human review of safety samples, limited pilot rollout.

Pinning & Deprecation process (summary):
- Pin request requires: customer justification, target CID (customer id), eval results proving stability, security sign-off, and release owner approval.
- Deprecation requires: compatibility matrix, migration path instructions, at least 30-day notice for enterprise customers or negotiated timelines for longer contracts.
- Automated tasks: create changelog entry, schedule rollout in Console, add fallback policies to ensure uninterrupted service.

Gates & Automation:
- Intake form will trigger automatic checks: license_scan (OSS license whitelist), model_size_check, architecture compatibility map, and an initial eval run on 1k prompts from our standard harness.
- If any gate fails, the ticket is routed to "Needs Investigation" with a required action by the requestor or engineering.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to close ticket):
- Published triage rubric and decision matrix in Confluence (owner: PM).
- Intake form template created in Forms + webhook to create Linear tickets with prefilled metadata.
- Automation: at least the license scan and initial eval run wired into the intake flow (proof-of-concept run for 3 real customer requests).
- Triage committee established (weekly 30-min) with defined roles and escalation paths.
- One pilot enterprise request handled through Fast-Track lane end-to-end (including pinning approval and Console rollout).

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Median time-to-decision for SLA-fasttrack requests <= 7 business days.
- % of catalog adds that pass automated pre-checks >= 60%.
- No customer incidents caused by missed pinning/deprecation notices.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Fast-Track increases operational cost; limit to customers above revenue/commit threshold.
- Aggressive automation might reject valid but unusual model families; maintain manual override path.
- Engineering capacity constraints for full eval runs; propose using sampling and staged runs to reduce load.
